Each subsidiary maintains its own separate legal personality, which is the cornerstone of the limited liability doctrine [cite: 10].

This separation ensures that the financial liabilities or legal disputes of one subsidiary—such as a data breach in the AI anti-phishing product or an infrastructure failure in the aerial fibre network—do not automatically jeopardize the capital of the holding company or other "sister" subsidiaries [cite: 6, 10]. However, this legal wall is not absolute; under Section 20(9) of the Companies Act, a court may "pierce the corporate veil" if the holding company is found to have abused the separate juristic personality of the subsidiary for fraudulent purposes [cite: 10].

## 3. Comprehensive Tax Implications and Group Relief Mechanisms

The fiscal health of an IT holding company is largely determined by its ability to utilize the tax relief provisions provided by the Income Tax Act (ITA). While South Africa does not permit consolidated tax filing for groups (each entity must file its own tax return at a 27% rate), the ITA offers several "Group Relief" provisions for companies within a 70% or greater shareholding relationship [cite: 11, 12].

### 3.1 Dividends Withholding Tax (DWT) Optimization
Profits generated by trading subsidiaries such as Bioniq are typically flowed upward to Veramani in the form of dividends. While dividends paid to individuals are subject to a 20% DWT, distributions to a South African tax-resident company are exempt [cite: 3, 13]. This international expansion is projected to generate significant revenue, with the cyber security division alone targeting over R28 million in income [cite: 22].

## 2. Bioniq (ISP): The Connectivity Backbone

Bioniq provides the mission-critical connectivity layer for the group’s industrial operations.
